title: Wait 10 s after the soldering iron is switched off, then box it within 25 s
instruction: The soldering iron is switched off while you watch. Do not touch it until 10 seconds after the light goes out, and have it in the tool box no later than 25 seconds after.
context: A hot tool looks like a cold one. The robot sees the moment the station is switched off and must count time from that event, with no clock in view, before touching the iron.
setup: On a wooden bench in front of two arms mounted 61 cm apart: a grey soldering station block (10 x 8 x 5 cm, fixed) 34 cm in front of the arm bases, 24 cm left of the centre line, carrying a red 1 cm cube on top as its power light; the soldering iron (dark plastic handle 12 x 2.2 x 2.2 cm with a 5 cm steel tip pointing away from the arms, 60 g) lying on the bench 22 cm out, 12 cm left of the centre line; an open blue tool box (22 x 10 cm, 6 cm walls) 15 cm out on the centre line. The robot is commanded from 1 s. At a moment between 1.5 s and 9 s that changes between trials (cycles through six values), the operator removes the red cube (the light goes out).
scoring: 0.33 when the iron is lifted 3 cm at or after 10 s past the light going out; 0.33 when it is inside the tool box (centre over the box floor, bottom within 2 cm of it); 0.34 when it rests in the box no later than 25 s after the light went out; success (1.0) when it rests there, in time, for 1 s. The score is set to 0 if, earlier than 10 s after the light went out, a fingertip (tool centre point) comes within 4 cm of the iron or the iron moves more than 1 cm. The episode ends with the score so far if 25 s pass without the iron resting in the box, or if the iron falls off the bench.
reset_notes: Lay the iron back on its spot, put the red cube on the station, empty the tool box; pick the next switch-off moment and remove the cube at that moment with a stopwatch.
fidelity: Approximate: no heat is simulated; the 'light' is a removable red cube; the iron is a rigid handle-plus-tip body.
